paras: Spending on finance automation by mid-sized European companies reached 4.1 billion euros in 2025, a rise of eleven per cent on the year before. The mid-market segment, companies with between 200 and 2,000 employees, now represents almost a third of total demand.

The main driver of this growth is the shift from manual invoice processing to automated matching. In our survey of 640 finance directors, 58 per cent of respondents said that the reduction of manual work was their first priority for 2026, ahead of cost reduction and compliance.

The integration of new tools with existing ERP systems remains the biggest barrier. Almost half of the respondents mentioned the complexity of the connection with SAP or Oracle as the reason for delaying a purchase. Vendors that offer a pre-built connection report a faster decision and a shorter sales cycle.

Market share is still concentrated: the three largest vendors hold 52 per cent of the market. However, their share fell by four points in 2025, mainly because of the arrival of smaller specialist vendors in Spain, Portugal and Eastern Europe.
We expect a growth rate of around nine per cent per year until 2028. The growth of demand will be strongest in the mid-market, where the adoption of automation is still below forty per cent.

items.situation: The report says: 'a rise of eleven per cent in spending'. Say it as a normal sentence on a call.
tips: Spending rose by eleven per cent.
The noun a rise becomes the verb rose; the amount still takes by.

items.situation: You want to write it in your slide title, report style. Turn 'demand grew strongly' into a noun phrase.
tips: Verb grew becomes noun growth; the adverb strongly becomes the adjective strong.

items.situation: Marta asks why the big vendors are losing share. Answer with the report.
tips: Their share fell by four points, mainly because of the arrival of smaller specialist vendors.
Because of + noun phrase: the arrival of...

items.situation: Marta asks what stops customers from buying. Answer in one sentence.
tips: The biggest barrier is the integration with SAP or Oracle.
The integration of X with Y: a noun with two prepositions.

items.situation: Say the main driver of growth as a full sentence a partner understands.
tips: Companies want to stop processing invoices by hand.
On a call, turn the heavy noun back into a verb: the reduction of manual work = they want less manual work.

items.situation: Marta asks: is the mid-market still growing? Answer with a number.
tips: Yes. The report expects a growth rate of about nine per cent a year until 2028.

listenings.text: I write market reports for a living, and I want to tell you a secret about them. They are written with nouns. A rise in spending. The growth of demand. The reduction of manual work. Nouns sound serious, and they let you put a lot of information into one line. But nobody talks like that. When you take a number from my report into a sales call, turn the noun back into a verb. Do not say there was an increase in the adoption of automation. Say more companies are automating. It is shorter, and people remember it. The other thing I always tell salespeople is to read the method before the headline. Who answered the survey? How many respondents? Which segment? A growth rate of nine per cent means one thing for a market of two hundred companies and something very different for a market of twenty thousand.

When a vendor shows me a market report in the first meeting, I usually stop listening. I do not need to hear that the market is growing. I can read that myself. What I need is one number from the report that is about me. For example, last month a vendor told me that almost half of finance directors delay a purchase because of the connection with SAP. Then he asked me if that was true for us. It was. That one number started a twenty-minute conversation about our real problem. So my advice is simple. Bring one number, not twenty. Say it in plain words. And then ask a question about my company, not about the market.
